name: Heiterwangsee
kurzbeschreibung: Lake Heiterwanger See at 976 metres near Reutte is a fjord-like mountain lake featuring crystalline waters, historic passenger boats, and a canal connecting to Lake Plansee.
preis: Lakeshore trails freely accessible; passenger ferry cruises and boat rentals apply fares
oeffnungszeiten: Lakeside trails open year-round; passenger boats operate late May to mid-October
beschreibung:
Überblick

The breathtaking Lake Heiterwanger See rests at an elevation of 976 metres, cradled between the precipitous forested flanks of the Ammergau and Lechtal Alps in the Tiroler Zugspitz Arena near Reutte. Connected to neighboring Lake Plansee via a 300-metre navigable canal, the two water bodies form a dramatic, fjord-like alpine lake system unparalleled in Austria. Covering approximately 137 hectares and descending to depths of 61 metres, Heiterwanger See captivates visitors with crystal-clear emerald waters fed by pristine mountain brooks. Dense spruce forests and sheer limestone ridges plunge directly into the mirror-calm surface, preserving an unspoiled wild ambiance. Recognized as one of Western Tirol's most scenic natural lakes, it pairs peaceful isolation with sustainable recreation. The lake is internationally renowned for its heritage passenger shipping: the motor vessels MS Margarethe and MS Wilhelm cruise both lakes in tandem, delivering a scenic fjord experience in the heart of the Alps.

Route & Anforderungen

A panoramic shoreline trail encircles Lake Heiterwanger See along a six-kilometre loop (approx. 1.5 to 2 hours walking time, 50 metres elevation gain). The path undulates through wooded bluffs, over timber footbridges, and along secluded pebble bays, revealing postcard-perfect vistas across the turquoise water. Long-distance hikers can expand their outing by combining both lakes on a grand 20-kilometre trek (approx. 5 to 6 hours), utilizing the passenger boat to shorten intermediate legs at will. Sturdy hiking shoes with lugged rubber soles are strongly advised, as narrow lakeside singletracks can become slick with tree roots after rain (unsuitable for pushchairs). Comfortable attire and sun protection are recommended.

Besuch & Anreise

Travel by road is toll-free from the German border via Füssen or Garmisch along federal highway B179 to the Heiterwang exit. Signposts lead directly to the lakeside Hotel Fischer am See, where paid parking is provided. Train travelers take the Außerfernbahn line to Heiterwang-Plansee station, reaching the lakeshore via a gentle twenty-minute walking path.

Tipps

Pair a morning shoreline walk with an afternoon cruise aboard the vintage passenger ships MS Margarethe or MS Wilhelm. During warm summer afternoons, quiet gravel coves on the southern shore provide refreshing wild swimming in pure drinking-quality alpine water. Electric motorboats and stand-up paddleboards are available for rent at the lakeside marina.
